content: Interventions for treating wrist fractures in children involve various approaches depending on the type, severity, and specific characteristics of the fracture. These may include non-surgical methods such as immobilization with a cast or splint, which is commonly used for stable fractures. Closed reduction, a procedure to realign the bones without surgery, may be necessary for displaced fractures before immobilization. In cases where non-surgical methods are insufficient, surgical interventions such as percutaneous pinning or open reduction with internal fixation may be required to ensure proper alignment and healing. Pain management, physical therapy, and regular follow-up imaging are also critical components of the treatment process to monitor healing and restore full function.
